title: Google Search Personal Intelligence Now Live Across Apps
summary: Google Search now integrates Personal Intelligence across Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Photos, and Wallet to deliver uniquely tailored search results.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Google Search now integrates Personal Intelligence to surface results from Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Photos, and Wallet in one unified experience.
- The system analyzes your personal data across Google apps to answer queries about reservations, documents, photos, and upcoming events automatically.
- Available immediately to all Google account holders with no additional setup required beyond existing app permissions and privacy controls.


Google Search has officially launched Personal Intelligence, a system-wide integration that connects search queries to personal data across Gmail,[Google Drive](https://emergent.sh/integrations/google-drive) ,[Google Calendar](https://emergent.sh/integrations/google-calendar) , Google Photos, and Google Wallet. The feature went live on November 23, 2026, fundamentally changing how the search engine surfaces information unique to each user's digital ecosystem.


## How Personal Intelligence Works


Personal Intelligence analyzes user data stored across Google's suite of applications to provide contextually relevant search results. When a user searches for "my flight details," the system automatically scans Gmail for confirmation emails, Calendar for itinerary events, and Wallet for boarding passes. Results appear in a unified interface that eliminates the need to manually check multiple apps.


The integration extends beyond travel queries. Users can search for "that spreadsheet from last week" and receive Drive results ranked by relevance and recency, or ask "when is my dentist appointment" to surface Calendar entries with location details pulled from Maps integration.


## Privacy Controls and Data Access


Google emphasizes that Personal Intelligence operates within existing privacy frameworks. Users maintain full control over which apps contribute data to search results through granular permission settings in their Google Account dashboard. The system respects existing sharing permissions, meaning work documents in a shared Drive folder remain visible only according to those access controls.


All personalized results appear only to the signed-in user and are not visible in incognito mode or when logged out. Google states that personal data used for search remains subject to the company's standard retention policies and is not used to train external AI models without explicit consent.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 23, 2026, Personal Intelligence rolled out automatically to all Google account holders worldwide. No manual activation is required beyond the existing permissions users have already granted to individual Google apps. The feature works across desktop web browsers, the Google mobile app on iOS and Android, and voice-activated searches through Google Assistant.


Google confirmed the rollout is complete as of this week, with server-side updates ensuring all users see the new functionality regardless of app version.


## Integration Scope and Supported Apps


The initial launch supports six core Google services: Gmail, Google Drive, Google Calendar, Google Photos, Google Wallet, and the base Google account profile. According to Google's announcement, additional integrations with Google Keep, Google Tasks, and Google Contacts are planned for a later 2026 release cycle.


The system also recognizes cross-app relationships. A search for "my vacation photos" might surface not only Photos results but also the original booking confirmation from Gmail and the calendar block showing travel dates, creating a comprehensive view of related information.


## What This Means


Personal Intelligence represents Google's most aggressive push yet to make search a central hub for personal information management. By connecting disparate data sources into a single query interface, the company aims to reduce app-switching friction and compete more directly with AI assistants from OpenAI and Anthropic that already offer cross-platform data synthesis. For users deeply embedded in the Google ecosystem, the feature transforms search from a web discovery tool into a personalized digital memory layer, though it also raises renewed questions about data consolidation and platform lock-in.
